pamphlet_excerpts: Standard Range Whistle Signals: The whistle commands used on a range, and their related verbal commands, are as follows (p. 11).
Two-Blast Line Approach: Two blasts on a whistle, "Step to the shooting line." You may step to the shooting line and pick up your bow (p. 11).
One-Blast Shooting Signal: One blast on a whistle, "Commence shooting." You may pick up an arrow and shoot this end (p. 11).
Bow Stand Waiting Protocol: When you are done, put your bow in a bow stand and step to the waiting line (p. 11).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Begin Shooting on One Blast: One blast on a whistle, "Commence shooting." You may pick up an arrow and shoot this end (p. 11).
Step 2 - Rack Bow and Step Back: When you are done, put your bow in a bow stand and step to the waiting line (p. 11).
Step 3 - Advance on Three Blasts: Three blasts on a whistle, "Retrieve your arrows." You may go downrange and retrieve your arrows (p. 11).
Step 4 - Pull Arrows Safely Downrange: Follow the three rules for retrieving arrows (above) (p. 11).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While shooting on the archery range, an arrow slips off your bow rest and lands on the ground 4 feet in front of the shooting line while other archers are still at full draw. What must you do?
quiz_item.question: While shooting on the archery range, an arrow slips off your bow rest and lands on the ground 4 feet in front of the shooting line while other archers are still at full draw. What must you do?
options: A. Lean forward across the shooting line and grab the arrow quickly before anyone notices.
B. Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.
C. Signal your buddy in the next lane to kick the arrow back behind the waiting line.
D. Use the tip of your unstrung bow limbs to hook the dropped arrow shaft while adjacent archers are releasing.
choices: A. Lean forward across the shooting line and grab the arrow quickly before anyone notices.
B. Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Stepping or reaching across an active shooting line puts you directly in the path of adjacent bows; any arrow forward of the line is retrieved only after all bows are racked on the 3-whistle signal.

requirements.req_text: Working under the supervision of a certified USA Archery Level 1 Instructor or a certified long-term camp staff member (i. e., a National Camping School [NCS] Range Activities Director; or a Rangemaster over age 18 who is trained by an NCS Range Activities Director or by a USA Archery Level 1 Instructor), do ONE of the following options: Note: When using a Genesis bow, apply the requirements in Option A. (a) Option A, Recurve Bow or Longbow. Do ALL of the following: (1) Name and point to the parts of the recurve or longbow you are shooting. (2) Explain how to properly care for and store recurve bows and longbows. (3) Demonstrate and explain USA Archery's 11 Steps of Shooting for the bow you are shooting. (4) Demonstrate the proper way to string a recurve bow or longbow. (5) Using a bow square, locate and mark with dental floss, crimp-on, or other method, the nocking point on the bowstring of the bow you are using. (6) Do ONE of the following: (a) Using a recurve bow or longbow and arrows with a finger release, shoot a single round of ONE of the following: (1) An NFAA field round of 14 targets and make a score of 60 points (2) A Scouting America field round of 14 targets and make a score of 80 points (3) A World Archery/USA Archery indoor round and make a score of 80 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (4) An NFAA indoor round and make a score of 50 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (b) Shooting 30 arrows in five-arrow ends at an 80-centimeter (32-inch) five-color target at 10 yards and using the 10 scoring regions, make a score of 150 points. (b) Option B, Compound Bow. Do ALL of the following: (1) Name and point to the parts of the compound bow you are shooting. (2) Explain how to properly care for and store compound bows. (3) Demonstrate and explain USA Archery's 11 Steps of Shooting for the bow you are shooting. (4) Explain why it is necessary to have the string or cable on a compound bow replaced at an archery shop. (5) Locate and mark with dental floss, crimp-on, or other method, the nocking point on the bowstring of the bow you are using. (6) Do ONE of the following: (a) Using a compound bow and arrows with a finger release, shoot a single round of ONE of the following: (1) An NFAA field round of 14 targets and make a score of 70 points (2) A Scouting America field round of 14 targets and make a score of 90 points (3) A World Archery/USA Archery indoor round and make a score of 90 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (4) An NFAA indoor round and make a score of 60 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (b) Shooting at an 80-centimeter (32-inch) five-color target using the 10 scoring regions, make a minimum score of 160 points. Accomplish this in the following manner: Shoot 15 arrows in five-arrow ends, at a distance of 10 yards AND Shoot 15 arrows in five-arrow ends, at a distance of 15 yards.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What must you do if you discover that one or more main strands of your bowstring are broken during your pre-shooting inspection?
quiz_item.question: What must you do if you discover that one or more main strands of your bowstring are broken during your pre-shooting inspection?
options: A. Wrap extra dental floss or serving thread tightly over the broken strands
B. Replace the entire bowstring before shooting the bow again
C. Rub extra bowstring wax into the broken strands to bind them together
D. Lower the bow's draw weight by twisting the string fewer times
choices: A. Wrap extra dental floss or serving thread tightly over the broken strands
B. Replace the entire bowstring before shooting the bow again
C. Rub extra bowstring wax into the broken strands to bind them together
D. Lower the bow's draw weight by twisting the string fewer times
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Replace the entire bowstring before shooting the bow again
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): If any main strands of a bowstring are broken, the string is weakened and could snap under tension, so the entire string must be replaced before shooting (p. 29).

options: A. Lean forward across the shooting line and grab the arrow quickly before anyone notices.
B. Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.
C. Signal your buddy in the next lane to kick the arrow back behind the waiting line.
D. Use the tip of your unstrung bow limbs to hook the dropped arrow shaft while adjacent archers are releasing.
choices: A. Lean forward across the shooting line and grab the arrow quickly before anyone notices.
B. Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.
C. Signal your buddy in the next lane to kick the arrow back behind the waiting line.
D. Use the tip of your unstrung bow limbs to hook the dropped arrow shaft while adjacent archers are releasing.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Stepping or reaching across an active shooting line puts you directly in the path of adjacent bows; any arrow forward of the line is retrieved only after all bows are racked on the 3-whistle signal.

options: A. To make the arrow drop rapidly within 30 yards like a flu-flu arrow
B. To prevent the arrow shaft from flexing when released from a heavy bow
C. To spin the arrow in flight and stabilize the broadhead point
D. To allow the arrow to pass cleanly through a whisker biscuit rest without touching
choices: A. To make the arrow drop rapidly within 30 yards like a flu-flu arrow
B. To prevent the arrow shaft from flexing when released from a heavy bow

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. To spin the arrow in flight and stabilize the broadhead point
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Target arrows use smaller feathers (2 to 3 inches) or plastic vanes (1.5 to 2 inches), whereas hunting arrows use 4 to 5 inch spiral fletchings to stabilize broadheads (p. 18).
